answer.rationale: The durable memory and experimental record strongly counsel against promotional_pricing as a response to competitive pressure: exp_73 showed that targeted discounting drives signup volume but destroys cohort retention (−12% at 30 days) and creates unsustainable revenue. Repeating that pattern under time pressure would worsen long-term qualified revenue, not maximize it. Instead, the data points toward a two-lever approach: (1) For price-sensitive SMB accounts at immediate churn risk, escalate to sales-assisted demo flows (memory_44 shows enterprise prospects convert better through demo paths and yield higher pipeline quality; this reduces pure price sensitivity by introducing higher-touch value communication). (2) Concurrently, activate referral incentive campaigns among established customers (memory_57 confirms referral performed well without retention harm, adding qualified revenue). This dual strategy avoids the retention cliff of discounting, shifts SMB value conversation upward through sales assistance, and leverages your existing customer base as a resilient acquisition channel. A standard_experiment on sales-assist for at-risk SMB accounts paired with referral activation among healthy accounts is lower-risk and aligns to sustainable growth. The enterprise lever also hedges against further SMB price competition by diversifying revenue mix.
